results.title: African climate negotiators warn against debt-driven energy transition ahead of COP31
results.content: The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) has warned that the global transition away from fossil fuels cannot be considered just if developing countries are forced to take on unsustainable debt to finance climate action. The group says mounting sovereign debt obligations are limiting the ability of African governments to invest in renewable energy, strengthen climate resilience and provide essential public services, despite the continent's relatively low contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions. The warning comes ahead of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled to take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, 2026.

results.title: The NPP’s politics of reporting Ghana and Africa to Western powers, a shameful legacy?
results.content: There is something deeply disturbing, disgraceful and profoundly disappointing about the New Patriotic Party's (NPP) decision to petition the United States to suspend diplomatic courtesies for Ghanaian diplomatic and service passport holders. It is difficult to understand how a political party that claims to have Ghana's best interests at heart can repeatedly resort to involving foreign powers in matters that Ghana's own institutions are constitutionally mandated to investigate. What exactly is wrong with the NPP? Have we reached a point where every domestic political disagreement must be carried to Washington for validation? Is Ghana no longer capable of investigating its own affairs? Must our sovereignty and international reputation become casualties of partisan bitterness?

results.title: Ghana Armed Forces physical training instructor criticises Sam George over confrontation with military officer
results.content: Physical Training Instructor Twumasi Barimah, popularly known as the Commander General of the Ghana Armed Forces, has criticised Communications Minister Samuel Nartey George over his handling of a confrontation with a military officer in the Ningo-Prampram Constituency. Mr Barimah said the minister, who is also the Member of Parliament for Ningo-Prampram, should have sought clarification about the military operation before publicly criticising the officer involved. He also questioned the minister's decision to disclose the officer's service number, arguing that his comments could incite residents against military personnel. Addressing the minister, Mr Barimah said his public remarks suggested that he had allowed his emotions to influence his response to the incident.

results.title: NACOC destroys seized drugs valued at over $10m at Bundase
results.content: More than US$10 million worth of seized narcotic substances have been taken out of circulation following a destruction exercise by the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) at Bundase. The consignment included millions of synthetic opioid tablets and capsules, thousands of bottles of codeine-based cough mixture and hundreds of kilogrammes of cannabis confiscated during anti-drug operations. Synthetic opioids accounted for the largest share of the drugs destroyed, with 4,730,100 capsules and tablets estimated to be worth US$5.9 million.

results.title: GHS directs health facilities to switch to paper reporting amid DHIMS2 shutdown
results.content: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has directed health facilities and districts nationwide to maintain paper-based reporting while its electronic health information systems remain unavailable. In an internal memo dated November 2, 2026, Director-General of the GHS, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, said the directive was intended to ensure that health data for October and November 2026 were preserved for entry once the systems are restored. “Facilities and districts should keep completing registers and monthly summary forms on paper so that October and November 2026 data can be entered once DHIMS2 is restored. Regional and district health information officers should file the forms by facility and month,” he stated.
